largestVariantRule: Take the 32-hex image hash and request it with NO size suffix from the CDN: https://s3-eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/loggia-cdn/lodgeContent/<hash>.jpg (<hash>.png for the header logo hash 3e3b5013ec554338704411496c011ec4). Strip any "_thumb" / "_square_thumb_<n>" suffix and any crawler "-<n>" mirror suffix first. The .webp forms (<hash>.webp / <hash>_thumb.webp) are same-dimension re-encodings, not larger renditions. The inflation comes from the same hash appearing as both a relative "../../../loggia-cdn/..." path and an absolute "https://s3-eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/loggia-cdn/..." URL, and in several size variants. "totalUnique" in this manifest counts unique files to download, not unique URL strings.

For 7 of the 673 CDN assets the crawl only ever exposed a "_thumb" URL, so the un-suffixed full-size "absoluteUrl" is INFERRED from the site-wide pattern and has not been verified (no network access was permitted): b622671c688bf1d7e961ee48e409f2e3, 14e77715b78ae6ce96ada21da4e1c939, 2119a061fcb9f948a11656d6c8a75ab0, b1bbe80a75b67db2c4370e62f6f836f3, ae3b9459e2e659faf3e93e5ab2e3e196, 2984622fa70b8aaa4796d646c5a7c6ea, df2bacefb7d7d5df11c75781c3e5249f. No image dimensions, byte sizes or MIME types are stated anywhere in the local sources, so none are recorded.

Most album/gallery images have alt text of the generic form "Album Image  #<id>" (note the double space between "Image" and "#", reproduced verbatim from the source) — these are not descriptive alts and will need real alt text written for the redesign.
The six villa hero-swiper slides and the six "Photo gallery" tiles on each villa page have NO alt attribute at all (alt is null in this manifest).
Home-page hero slides only carry placeholder alts "Jumbotron-Img-1" .. "Jumbotron-Img-6"; the villa teaser cards only carry "Gallery-Photo-1" .. "Gallery-Photo-7". No descriptive alt exists for them.

Home-page experience card "A Moment of Fairytale" (hash 2984622fa70b8aaa4796d646c5a7c6ea) has no corresponding crawled detail page, so its experience slug was derived from the card alt text ("a-moment-of-fairytale") rather than from a real URL.

Home-page amenity cards "Private Beach", "Playground and vegetable garden", "Breakfast", "Doctor" and "Babysitter" have no crawled detail page (only /en/article/1899 "Sitting outdoor area" was crawled), so their amenity slugs were derived from the card alt text.

Every villa detail page (/en/property/200, /201, /202, /203, /2142, /en/thalasses-rituals, /en/villa-pueblo) embeds the same Google Maps iframe (https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!...!2sThalasses!5e1!...). It is a third-party embed, not a downloadable asset, so it is listed neither under "videos" nor under "assets".
The three YouTube embeds have no title attribute, caption or transcript in the source, so "videos" entries carry no human-readable title.

root.html and en__index-1.htm (and en__index-1.htm_q_x=1) are the same home page crawled at different URLs; root.html declares og:url "https://thalasses.com/" while en__index-1.htm declares "https://thalasses.com/en/". All three were collapsed to "https://thalasses.com/en/" in usedOnPages.

Villa entity folders use the CMS property ids seen in the URLs: 200 = Villa Thoi, 201 = Villa Persi, 202 = Villa Eeanthe, 203 = Villa Melia, 2142 = Thalasses Villas (the whole estate listing). Thalasses Rituals and Villa Pueblo have slug URLs instead of numeric ids and are foldered by slug.
Where a hash appears on both a specific villa page and the /property/2142 estate listing, it was attributed to the specific villa; assets seen ONLY on 2142 are foldered under villas/2142.
The site host name is not stated in the mirrored relative paths; the cdnBase value is reconstructed from the absolute S3 URLs that appear alongside them in the same pages.

The non-CDN path /assets/images/mailia/Out_1_11.jpg uses the spelling "mailia" while the villa is presented on the site as "Villa Melia"; /assets/images/eanthe/ likewise vs "Villa Eeanthe". Spellings left exactly as found.
Album image alt ids (e.g. "Album Image  #26235") are CMS internal ids; they were not used for naming because they are not stable content identifiers.
